title: Projection-formula coherence for a square of ringed topoi
statement:
Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_X)$, $(\mathcal Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, $(\mathcal X',\mathcal O_{X'})$, and $(\mathcal Y',\mathcal O_{Y'})$ be ringed topoi, with morphisms $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$, $f':\mathcal X'\to\mathcal Y'$, $g:\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$, $g':\mathcal X'\to\mathcal X$ and a specified commutation isomorphism $f g'\cong g f'$ of ringed-topos morphisms (compatible with the structure-ring maps). Use sites small in the chosen universe, their unbounded derived categories of module sheaves, the canonical derived module pullback and tensor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and derived direct images with their canonical adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ for the four edges. Let $\theta: L(f')^*Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g')^*Lf^*$ be the pullback comparison induced by this ringed commutation isomorphism. Define $\pi_u$ to be the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_{u,E}\otimes1)\circ t_u$, where $t_u:Lu^*(V\otimes^L W)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*V\otimes^LLu^*W$ is the canonical tensor comparison; define $\operatorname{Ex}$ to be the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $\theta$. For $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $Q\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$, let $\pi_f$ be the projection-formula map (the mate of counit tensor identity), and let $\operatorname{Ex}$ be the exchange map (the mate of the commutation isomorphism). The two composites
$$
Lg^*(Rf_*E\otimes^L Q)\xrightarrow{Lg^*\pi_f} Lg^*Rf_*(E\otimes^L Lf^*Q)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}} Rf'_*L(g')^*(E\otimes^L Lf^*Q)
$$
and
$$
Lg^*(Rf_*E\otimes^L Q)\cong Lg^*Rf_*E\otimes^L Lg^*Q\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}\otimes1} Rf'_*L(g')^*E\otimes^L Lg^*Q\xrightarrow{\pi_{f'}}Rf'_*(L(g')^*E\otimes^L L(f')^*Lg^*Q)
$$
are equal after the canonical derived pullback tensor and composition identifications of the targets. This holds without a cartesianness assumption on the square and is natural in $E,Q$.

proof.text: Put $F=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$, $B=Lg^*$, $C=L(f')^*$, $S=Rf'_*$, and $H=L(g')^*$. Write $t_U:U(V\otimes W)\to UV\otimes UW$ for the canonical comparisons; all tensors in this proof are derived. Construct the natural isomorphism $\theta:CB\to HF$ on K-flat representatives with flat terms: choose such a representative by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; successive ordinary module pullbacks compute successive derived pullbacks by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and remain K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Ordinary composition is scalar-extension associativity: $S_2\otimes_{u^{-1}S_1}u^{-1}(S_1\otimes_{v^{-1}R}v^{-1}P)\cong S_2\otimes_{(vu)^{-1}R}(vu)^{-1}P$, sending $s\otimes(a\otimes p)$ to $s\,u^{-1}(a)\otimes p$, with inverse $s\otimes p\mapsto s\otimes(1\otimes p)$. Apply this to the two composites and the given ringed commutation isomorphism. The resulting complex isomorphisms are natural, preserve degrees and commute with differentials. Localization on the resolving subcategory is equivalent to the derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], so these isomorphisms define $\theta$ for every derived object, independently of the chosen representative. This is the explicit representative construction of Tag 0D6D; it requires no coefficient-ring isomorphism on the individual edges.

The comparison $\theta$ respects tensor in the following precise form, for $V,W\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$:
$$t_H\,H(t_F)\,\theta_{V\otimes W}=(\theta_V\otimes\theta_W)\,t_C\,C(t_B).$$
To check this, use flat K-flat representatives for $V,W$. The canonical module comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] is the balanced map $s\otimes(v\otimes w)\mapsto(s\otimes v)\otimes(1\otimes w)$; its inverse multiplies the two scalars. The composition comparison of Step 1 multiplies nested scalars. Thus splitting a tensor before or after composing pullbacks gives the same map: each outer scalar goes to the first factor, each second-factor scalar is moved across the balanced tensor relation, and both routes multiply the same scalar images. The ringed commutation isomorphism identifies those scalar images, and its inverse-image comparison sends a pair of sections to the pair of their images. Hence both routes agree on pure tensors and, by additivity and the balanced relations, on module sheaves. In the total tensor complexes they preserve the bidegrees, so no permutation or extra sign occurs. The derived comparison is the class of precisely these module comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; natural transformations extend uniquely in the two K-flat variables by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. This proves the displayed equality on arbitrary $V,W$.

proof.text:
Let $\varepsilon:FR\to1$ and $\varepsilon':CS\to1$ be the counits of the given adjunctions. By the definition of mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], for $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ the transpose of $\operatorname{Ex}_E:BRE\to SHE$ is
$$\delta_E:=\varepsilon'_{HE}\,C(\operatorname{Ex}_E)=H(\varepsilon_E)\,\theta_{RE}:CBRE\to HE.$$
By the definition of the projection map in the statement,
$$\varepsilon_{E\otimes FQ}\,F(\pi_{f,E,Q})=(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\,t_F.$$
These identities follow from the adjunction triangle identity: for any $a:LA\to D$, its adjunct is $R(a)\eta_A$, and $\varepsilon_D L(R(a)\eta_A)=a\varepsilon_{LA}L\eta_A=a$. Thus equality of the desired maps can be tested by their transposes under $C\dashv S$.

proof.text:
Write $U=RE$ and $N=E\otimes FQ$. Identify the final object on $X'$ with $HE\otimes CBQ$ using $t_H$ and $1\otimes\theta_Q^{-1}$. The transpose of the first composite is
$$a=(1\otimes\theta_Q^{-1})\,t_H\,H(\varepsilon_N)\,\theta_{RN}\,CB(\pi_{f,E,Q}).$$
Naturality of $\theta$ for $\pi_{f,E,Q}:U\otimes Q\to RN$ replaces the last two factors by $HF(\pi_{f,E,Q})\theta_{U\otimes Q}$. The projection transpose identity of Step 3 and naturality of $t_H$ then give
$$a=(H\varepsilon_E\otimes\theta_Q^{-1})\,t_H\,H(t_F)\,\theta_{U\otimes Q}.$$
Every factor here has source $CB(U\otimes Q)$ and final target $HE\otimes CBQ$; no projection-formula isomorphism is assumed.

proof.text:
The transpose of the second composite is, by the defining projection transpose at $f'$ and the naturality of $t_C$,
$$b=(\varepsilon'_{HE}\otimes1)\,t_C\,C(\operatorname{Ex}_E\otimes1)\,C(t_B)
=(\delta_E\otimes1)\,t_C\,C(t_B).$$
Insert Step 2 with $(V,W)=(U,Q)$ in the expression for $a$. Functoriality of tensor and $\theta_Q^{-1}\theta_Q=1$ yield
$$a=(H\varepsilon_E\,\theta_U\otimes1)\,t_C\,C(t_B)
=(\delta_E\otimes1)\,t_C\,C(t_B)=b.$$
Since transposition is bijective (Step 3), the two original composites are equal. Their naturality in $E,Q$ follows directly from naturality of $t$, $\theta$, counits and adjuncts; alternatively the same transpose identities for morphisms in each variable prove the naturality squares. Only the ringed commutation isomorphism has been used, so no cartesianness, flatness, properness, boundedness, or perfectness hypothesis enters.
